action_items: Investigate why stubInlineTap results in two toast() invocations per single click. Likely culprits: (a) React 18 StrictMode double-invocation in dev; (b) toast fired both from onClick AND some other handler (verify no onMouseUp/onPointerUp path); (c) sonner duplicate-insert when the panel re-renders between click dispatch and toast state update. Suggested fix: inside stubInlineTap, in addition to the ref guard, dedupe via toast id, e.g. toast.message('...', { id: 'ir-inline-align-coming-soon' }) so sonner collapses duplicates.

rca of the issue: Suspected root cause of the duplicate toast: either React 18 StrictMode double-invocation of the onClick handler in development build, or the fact that both the AlignPanel wrapper and the overlay portal are mounted in the DOM subtree and each may be re-triggering synthetic click events. The useRef guard inside stubInlineTap short-circuits only on the SECOND invocation per component instance; if the component re-renders between the two invocations the ref would still persist, so the two toasts most likely come from two synchronous calls within one event tick before the ref flip takes effect — but useRef write is synchronous, so this is unlikely. More likely: onClick is being dispatched twice (either React dev-mode or a bubbled click reaching an ancestor). Mitigation: pass a stable `id` to the sonner `toast.message(...)` call so sonner deduplicates even if invoked twice.
